Blackwing Pencil Essentials Set Review — Supply Atelier

 

# Blackwing Pencil Essentials Set 

 Some tools become favorites because the experience of using them is simply better. Blackwing pencils fit that idea particularly well: distinctive, beautifully made and designed for people who still value drawing and thinking on paper. We chose the Essentials Set because it lets you try all four of Blackwing’s core graphite options before deciding which suits your way of working. It also includes the One-Step Long Point Sharpener and Point Guard, making it a compact, well-designed analogue toolkit rather than just a box of pencils. 

Contents

Matte: Soft graphite Pearl: Balanced graphite 602: Firm graphite Natural: Extra-firm graphite

Packaging

 Presented as a boxed set

## The short version

What works

- Four graphite grades to experiment with
- Excellent for finding your preferred Blackwing pencil
- Long-point sharpener included
- Point Guard is genuinely useful when travelling
- Distinctive, sophisticated industrial design
- Makes an excellent gift for a designer or illustrator

What to know

- Expensive compared with conventional graphite pencils
- Only one pencil of each graphite grade
- Specialized accessories add cost if you only want the pencils
- More of an introduction to Blackwing than a long-term pencil supply

## In use

The real advantage of this set is choice. Designers use pencils differently: a softer line can be ideal for expressive sketching and shading, while firmer graphite works better for precise diagrams, notes and controlled linework. Having all four Blackwing cores side by side makes those differences immediately useful.

The included sharpener is also more than an accessory. Blackwing’s One-Step Sharpener creates a long, curved point designed to resist breakage, while the aluminum Point Guard protects the sharpened pencil when carried in a bag or pencil case. 

Aesthetically, the set is excellent. The pencils retain Blackwing’s recognizable rectangular ferrule and understated finishes, while the black accessories make the collection feel coherent without becoming overly precious.

At around $50, however, this is unquestionably a premium stationery purchase. You can sketch perfectly well with far cheaper pencils. The value comes from the combination of graphite quality, design, accessories and the pleasure of using a thoughtfully designed everyday object.

results.title: Doctor, I Need Pencil-cillin: Mega Blackwing Pencil Test! – Nib & Muck
results.author: nibandmuck
results.text:
Doctor, I Need Pencil-cillin: Mega Blackwing Pencil Test! – Nib & Muck

 

# Doctor, I Need Pencil-cillin: Mega Blackwing Pencil Test!

Do not adjust your screens. I actually AM talking about pencils today, not pens. Don’t shoot me.

BUT, I’ve found that pencils are equally as nuanced, beautiful and interesting as fountain pens. I know, I was shocked to the core too (like the pencil pun ;)?!). Sometimes, a pen just won’t cut it and the archival, erasable and instantaneous quality of a pencil is what you need. Like drawing a mark on wood. Or jotting down a shopping list on crap paper in a hurry. Or stabbing your enemy in the eye. PENCILS WILL DO THIS!

So, when the lovely Mishka at Bureau Direct asked me if I wanted to try a selection of their Blackwing range I jumped at the chance, despite the fountain pen part of my brain screaming ‘NOOOoooOOOOO!’

Here are my layman thoughts on these Blackwing Beauties. Erasable Podcast Boys eat your heart out!

A gaggle of Blackwings

## Intravenous Drip: Palomino Handheld Sharpener

In case you aren’t aware (or have the IQ of a gnat), you need a decent sharpener to get a killer point on your pencil, much like an intravenous drip of blood to keep you alive. The Palomino Handheld Sharpener made by Kum is an incredible example. It comes with two holes: one to sharpen the wood into a long cone, and one to sharpen the lead into the LONGEST POINT EVER! Such a simple but well put together tool, this sharpener was easy to use and delivered amazing points every time. My only gripe is that it didn’t hold a high volume of shavings; after one pencil I was frantically searching for a bin whilst ruining my carpet with off cuts. Nevertheless, a must have for pencil aficionados on the go…if you think £10.95 is reasonable for a sharpener.

 

 

 

 

Look at the points on that!

Here come the pencils in order of firmness, starting with the limited edition 530 at the firmest end of the scale for writing, through to the Classic at the softer end of the scale for sketching. Look at me being all official and that!

## The New Registrar: Blackwing 530

First up and – just to spoil it – my absolute favourite of the bunch is the 530. As a Blackwing limited edition, it commemorates a key moment or figure in American history because…well it’s hipster as f**k, isn’t it? The 530 represents James Marshall discovering gold in California in 1848, hence the Goldfinger style paint job. It has an extra-firm graphite core, and I LOVED the way it wrote. Super smooth, great point retention and little smudging if you smeared your greasy paws all over it accidentally. The rubber on the end wasn’t too bad either, removing most of the pencil mark after a few swipes. I’m not mad keen on the gold finish as it makes me look like a pretentious tit when using it, but I am happy to endure this social labelling just for the writing experience.

4 pencil-cillin pills out of 5

The Hipster Beast. Image courtesy of Blackwing602.com

## The Sexy Nurse: Blackwing 602

Everyone worth their stationery salt has tried one of these. The 602 is made of incense cedar (so smells DIVINE!), has a super-cool grey and gold finish and is the flagship Blackwing model. It’s firm yet smooth core promises to deliver ‘half the pressure, twice the speed’ and it does so with aplomb. I enjoyed writing with it, but preferred the darker, firmer line of the 530 for everyday writing. The 602 was a touch too soft and light for me, but is a great all rounder for writing and sketching if that is your thing. Not a bad pencil at all…just not a 530.

3.5 pencil-cillin pills out of 5

Smeary comparisons

## The Hassled Doctor: Blackwing Pearl

Another of Palomino’s standard models, is the Blackwing Pearl. It is much softer than the 602, and puts down the darkest line of the bunch. I liked how dark it wrote, and it was awesome for underlining in books due to its boldness. I also adore the finish; as a recovering Apple whore, the simple white and black lines really turn me on. It is my second favourite of the bunch; only pipped by the 530 as the Pearl is so ridiculously soft, I was sharpening it every couple of lines to keep a decent point. Will be a firm favourite in my pencil case.

3.75 pencil-cillin pills out of 5

## The Hospital Janitor: Blackwing Classic

Finally, my least favourite of the Blackwing gaggle, the Classic. It is soft as sh*t, more boring than a party political broadcast in terms of looks (it’s plain black), and is a NIGHTMARE to erase. I didn’t enjoy it for writing as it smudged all over the place, BUT I can see the merits of it for sketching and shading. Its ‘smudgeability’ lends itself well to artistic pieces and it lays down a dark line. I also liked the look of the white eraser…but alas, it couldn’t even erase invisible lines ;)! Not a crap pencil by any means, just not to my taste.

2 pencil-cillin pills out of 5

Analog versus digital

## Final Diagnosis

I can’t believe it. I have to admit that I like – no more than that – REALLY LIKE pencils. They are as idiosyncratic as pens and provide an equally diverse writing experience. Overall, I’ve loved the Blackwing selection I received to test. They look awesome (and appeal to my inner hipster toff), have good point retention and lay down amazingly dark lines with a wonderful writing experience. Another added bonus: they smell delicious when sharpened.

Big thanks to Bureau Direct for providing this test sample free of charge (although all opinions are my own). You can pick up a box of 12 of each of these Blackwings for £24.95 (excluding the 530 limited edition). Check out their website for the latest Blackwing offerings and subscribe to their newsletter for a 10% discount code every month. BOOM!

> ### Have you ever ventured to the graphite dark side?!

Keep those nibs (or should I say points?!) mucky!

Blackwing Pencils: A Comprehensive Guide | JetPens

# Blackwing Pencils: A Comprehensive Guide

October 21, 2025 - Posted by Connie to Guides, Pencils, Wooden Pencils

When you try a Blackwing, you’ll know why artists and writers are obsessed with this graphite pencil. Read on to learn why Blackwing Pencils stand out and see limited edition pencils you’ll want to collect.

Table of Contents

- Blackwing Characteristics
- Standard Blackwing Pencils
- Other Blackwing Pencils
- Blackwing Gift Sets

Form Factor

Blackwing Pencils are known for their flat ferrules.

 Blackwing Pencils have distinctive looks that set them apart from other pencils. Their iconic ferrules (the metal parts at the opposite ends of the graphite) are long and flat. They hold rectangular erasers that can be extended with the metal clips when they wear down, and replaced when they’re used up. 

Blackwing Pencils have unique eraser clips and erasers. They’re also longer than typical pencils.

 The graphite pencils have gold-colored ferrules, while the colored pencils have silver ferrules. The included rubber erasers are black for the Matte, white for the Pearl, pink for the 602, and gray for the Natural. The Colors have gray sand erasers. 

The Matte, Pearl, and 602 models are finished with black, white, or gray lacquer. The Natural has a clear finish so you can see the wood’s texture. The Colors have barrels that match the cores. The Blackwing logo and pencil’s name is gold foiled into the side of each pencil.

Blackwing Pencils are longer than typical pencils, so they don’t fit in standard pen cases. All of the cases in our Extra Long Pencil Cases category can fit Blackwing Pencils.

Lead Grades

Blackwing graphite ranges from soft to extra firm.

 Unlike most brands that use European or American lead grades, Blackwing has four proprietary lead grades, listed below: 

- Soft: The softest and darkest Blackwing graphite. It’s like 3B lead.
- Balanced: Blackwing’s balanced graphite is similar to 2B lead.
- Firm: Firm lead is similar in feel to B lead.
- Extra Firm: The hardest graphite Blackwing offers. It’s the most similar to #2 or HB pencil lead.

Other lead grades are sometimes made for limited edition releases. Check out the Volumes or Special Editions sections to learn more.

Materials

A Blackwing Pencil has a pleasant smell thanks to its incense cedar body.

 All Blackwing Pencils are made from California incense cedar. They have mild, pleasant scents that get stronger when the pencils are sharpened. 

The graphite and wax cores are made in Japan. The graphite uses a formula that’s smoother and softer than most pencil leads. However, they hold their points reasonably well.

Standard Blackwing Pencils

Blackwing Matte Pencils

The Blackwing Matte uses soft and dark graphite.

Blackwing Matte Pencils use the softest and darkest lead. Their buttery cores feel similar to 3B leads and are especially good for art. They can make light marks when used with a gentle touch, but are typically quite dark. Unlike some soft pencils, the Matte Pencils don’t crumble with use. They’re very consistent and sharpen to fine points, but because they’re so soft, they wear down quickly. 

The original Matte Pencils have black bodies with gold-colored ferrules and black erasers. The Green Finish and Red Finish Pencils have copper-colored ferrules and gray erasers.

Graphite: Soft (similar to 3B lead)

Blackwing Pearl Pencils

The Blackwing Pearl stays sharp longer than the Matte Pencil.

 The Blackwing Pearl is a bit harder than the Blackwing Matte, but it’s still soft and dark. It stays sharp longer, so people who enjoy smooth pencils but don’t want to sharpen them as often will prefer the Pearl. Its balance of darkness and hardness makes it a great option for people who want to use the same pencil to write and draw with. 

The original Blackwing Pearl has a pearlescent white finish with a gold ferrule and white eraser. It’s also available with shimmery pink or blue barrels.

Graphite: Balanced (similar to 2B lead)

Blackwing 602 Pencils

The Blackwing 602 is closest to the original Blackwing.

 Ideal for writing, the Blackwing 602 is smoother than a typical writing pencil. It’s the closest in feel to the vintage Eberhard Faber Blackwing. As a tribute, it has the original “Half the Pressure, Twice the Speed” slogan on the barrel. 

The Blackwing 602 has a pearlescent gray finish with a gold ferrule and pink eraser. You can also get them as short pencils that are half the length of the standard 602, so they fit right into pencil cases without needing to wear them down first.

Graphite: Firm (similar to B lead)

Blackwing Natural Pencils

The Blackwing Natural offers the hardest graphite found in the standard Blackwing lineup.

 The newest addition to the standard lineup, the Blackwing Natural Pencil offers the hardest graphite. They’re still smooth, which makes writing with them a pleasant experience. We recommend them to writers who want their pencils to stay sharp as long as possible. 

They’re unpainted with clear matte finishes, letting you appreciate the natural color and pattern of the wood.

Graphite: Extra Firm (similar to HB lead)

Blackwing Colors Colored Pencils

 Blackwing Colors have extra-smooth wax cores.

Blackwing Colors are colored pencil versions of Blackwing Pencils. Their extra smooth wax cores don’t feel “waxy” or become crumbly with use. They’re made from California incense cedar with cores made in Japan. 

The colored pencils include special sand erasers made specifically for the Blackwing’s color cores.

They work best on mildly textured paper, like the kind found in adult coloring books. They also show up well on black paper.

Blackwing Non-Photo Blue & Red Pencils

Blackwing Non-Photo Blue & Red Pencils have useful colored cores.

 These pencils combine the iconic aesthetics of Blackwing Pencils with useful colored cores. The Non-Photo Blue Pencils create light blue lines that won’t appear on scans or photocopies. They can also be removed easily using digital art software. 

The Red Pencils leave vivid marks that are excellent for edits and corrections. Both pencils have colored sand erasers and are available in packs of six.

Blackwing Box Sets

 Blackwing Box Sets are made of luxurious materials and filled with Blackwing Pencils.

 A Blackwing Box Set is a lovely present for a fellow writer or pencil enthusiast—it’s also a great way to treat yourself! The boxes are made from different materials and include twelve pencils. The pencils can be the same types, or you can get mixed varieties. 

The Rustic boxes also include Two-Step Long Point Sharpeners.

Blackwing Volumes Vol. 292 Pencils

 Keith Haring was one of the most influential young artists of the 1980s. When he opened his Pop Shop in 1986, Haring thought of it as a physical extension of his work, a place where everyone was welcome to experience his art. Printed with his iconic colorful dancing figures, Blackwing Volumes Vol. 292 Pencils are tributes to Keith and his enduring legacy. The volume number is a reference to 292 Lafayette Street, the address of his original Pop Shop in SoHo, Manhattan. 

A matching One-Step Long Point Pencil Sharpener and Point Guard Pencil Cap are also available.

Blackwing Volumes Vol. 574 Pencils

 These Vol. 574 Pencils are tributes to Native American art and the 574 surviving tribes within the United States. Designed in collaboration with Chris Papaan, a Kaw, Osage, and Lakota artist, they feature geometric patterns evocative of the patterns found in the art of many Native American tribes. Blackwing will donate a portion of the proceeds from this release to the Cheyenne River Youth Project and their mission to provide enriching arts programs to Lakota youth. 

Blackwing Volumes Vol. XIX Second Edition Pencils

Blackwing Volumes Vol. XIX Second Edition Pencils

 These Vol. XIX Pencils are re-releases of pencils from 2020. They celebrate the ratification of the 19th Amendment, which gave women of the United States the right to vote throughout the country, and the ongoing fight to protect voting rights in the United States and around the world. 

Graphite: Extra Firm

Blackwing Volumes Vol. 71 Pencils

Blackwing Volumes Vol. 71 Pencils

Vol. 71 Pencils are tributes to the modernist architect Frank Lloyd Wright and his architectural vision. Each pencil has one of four designs based on the perforated window boards commonly found in his iconic Usonian houses. The designs are printed in a muted, mid-century color palette, with the pencils’ natural wood finish showing through the negative space. The number 71 refers to Wright’s age when he constructed his first Usonian home. 

Graphite: Extra Firm

Blackwing Volumes Vol. 746 Pencils

 Though many thought the construction of a bridge across the Golden Gate Strait was impossible, a dauntless team of engineers and designers exceeded every challenge.
